label: GBIF Occurrence API (occurrence/count and occurrence/search?limit=0 count queries against the GBIF occurrence index)

not_verified_from_this_host.note: www.gbif.org answers HTTP 403 to non-browser clients (confirmed again on 2026-10-31 with curl, with and without a browser User-Agent), so the following pages could not be fetched and are listed only because the techdocs pages above link to them as 'Terms and agreements' and 'citation guidelines'. They are not cited as verified.

governance: GBIF is an intergovernmental infrastructure: Participants (countries, economies and international organisations) sign the GBIF Memorandum of Understanding and are represented on the GBIF Governing Board; the Secretariat in Copenhagen operates the index (docs.gbif.org effective-nodes-guidance, section 1). Occurrence records are published by registered publishers as Darwin Core Archives (or BioCASe/TAPIR/DiGIR), crawled, interpreted and flagged by a documented pipeline (techdocs data-processing, ingestion-steps). Each publishing dataset carries one of three licences (CC0 1.0, CC BY 4.0, CC BY-NC 4.0), exposed per dataset in the registry API field `license`; an aggregate count therefore has a mixed licence. Users of downloads agree to cite a DOI under the data user agreement (techdocs data-use/citation).
versioning: Live index with no snapshot identifier for a count query. Counts change continuously as datasets are crawled, re-interpreted or deleted: on 2026-10-31 the global index (`GET /v1/occurrence/count` with no filter) reported 3,887,217,103 records across 54,172 occurrence datasets. Only occurrence *downloads* receive a DOI and are frozen; a `occurrence/count?taxonKey=K` or `occurrence/search?taxonKey=K&limit=0` response is a point-in-time number whose only version is the retrieval timestamp. Taxon keys used as filters are GBIF Backbone usage keys (checklistKey defaults to the backbone, d7dddbf4-2cf0-4f39-9b2a-bb099caae36c); GBIF states that backbone identifiers will be preserved and supported in the API (techdocs data-processing/taxonomy-interpretation).
known_issues: A count query has no persistent identifier and cannot be frozen; reproducibility is only approximate (drift of a few records per day for most taxa, more for taxa with large citizen-science inflow). The project tolerance (relative <= 0.5% or absolute <= 5) absorbs this for most taxa for a few days, not indefinitely.

The count response (`occurrence/count`) is a bare integer, so its SHA-256 changes whenever the count changes; the `occurrence/search?limit=0` response additionally carries volatile ordering of facets/fields, so a checksum mismatch on these distributions is expected and is not by itself an integrity failure.

Counts include every basis of record (preserved specimens, human observations, machine observations, fossil specimens, material citations, living specimens) and every descendant taxon of the key, including synonyms matched to the key; they are a sampling-effort proxy, not an abundance or range measure. Records with coordinate issues are included unless the query says `hasCoordinate=true&hasGeospatialIssue=false`.

Duplicate publication of the same specimen or observation by more than one publisher is common (GBIF flags clusters but does not remove them from counts), so constituent records are not fully independent of one another.

Several higher-rank backbone keys are orphaned or non-accepted in the frozen 2023-08-28 backbone: a count under such a key can be far below the biological group's real coverage (verified 2026-10-31: Reptilia 358 is a PROPARTE_SYNONYM with numDescendants 0; Marsupialia 9712517 is ranked FAMILY with 15 descendants; Crustacea and Vertebrata have no accepted usage, so vendors used sets of component orders instead). A zero or tiny count for a key above species rank is a sign of such a key, not of absence of data.
The public landing pages `https://www.gbif.org/occurrence/search?taxon_key=K` return HTTP 403 to automated clients, so identifier resolution has to be verified through the equivalent API URL.

The GBIF backbone build has been discontinued in favour of the Catalogue of Life eXtended Release (COL XR); counts by backbone key will remain stable in semantics, but newly described taxa are only reachable via `checklistKey=7ddf754f-d193-4cc9-b351-99906754a03b`.
rationale: Source authority 0.9: GBIF is the canonical example of a governed international infrastructure named in the rubric's 1.0 anchor, with a documented processing pipeline, an OpenAPI specification and published source code; the deduction is because the artefact actually vendored here, a live count, has no DOI, no snapshot and no versioning beyond its retrieval timestamp (DOIs exist only for downloads). Independence 0.85: the occurrence index is produced by tens of thousands of publishers with no relation to this project or its claims, but it is an aggregation in which constituent records are known to overlap (re-published specimens, citizen-science platforms exposed through several publishers), which is the situation the rubric's 0.5 anchor points at, weighed against the fact that overlap is small relative to counts of this size. Authenticity 1.0: the counts are real server-side aggregates over observed and specimen records, reproducible from the recorded URLs, and there are no templated or synthetic components in the source itself.
